description: Curated HelioClock release highlights; add one entry whenever the application version changes. README milestone table is generated from these entries.

releases.summary: Add Sun motion trails to Sky Compass and all Earth projections: fixed-UTC annual analemma, manual time-step breadcrumbs, independent dots/line styling, synchronized panel controls and clear trail.
Show substantially more lunar names at low magnification by relaxing zoom eligibility and scaling collision-limited label density to the viewport, while preserving the 500-feature searchable atlas.

Expand the lunar atlas to 500 searchable named features: retain 115 curated landmarks, add 385 prominent near-side craters from USGS-derived nomenclature data, and maintain zoom-dependent uncluttered labels.

Curated 115-feature near-side lunar atlas with zoom-aware collision-limited labels, maria/crater/other filters, searchable names, centering and selection; fixed mosaic coordinates are explicitly approximate, with libration deferred.
Replace 100 minor-planet diamond markers with small hollow circles (selected body enlarged), and extend optional ecliptic height risers to visible planets, with numeric planet height in inspection.
100 searchable diameter-ranked numbered minor planets from NASA/JPL; low-cost markers, selective orbit paths, labels for the primary four and the selected body.
Inspect selected comet/asteroid inclination, eccentricity, perihelion and aphelion, ascending node, and signed ecliptic height; optionally show a 3D drop line to the ecliptic plane.
Click or tap Orrery planet, asteroid, or selected-comet markers for a synchronized object selection, highlighting, heliocentric distance and date readout; gestures still rotate without selecting.
Synchronize numeric Orrery camera angles with mouse/touch dragging and reset, while allowing direct gestures across the full ±180° tilt range.
Label all four minor bodies in the Orrery, extend 3D tilt through ±180°, show editable tilt/rotation degrees, and optionally draw a faint ecliptic reference mesh.

Add independent Orrery minor-body controls to toggle all four JPL asteroids, choose one directly, search for any bundled MPC comet, show/hide comet orbit guides, and clear selections without leaving the Orrery.
Add JPL SBDB-backed Ceres, Pallas, Juno and Vesta search and approximate positions, optional purple asteroid markers and orbits in the Sky Compass and Orrery.
Add Clear selection to restore an unselected Sky Compass and Orrery; generate an offline, explicitly caveated JPL Horizons XYZ comparison for Halley at 1986, 2026, and 2061 in each packaged build.
Plot the selected comet's approximate heliocentric orbit and position in the Orrery with a Fit selected comet control, and keep Sky Compass grid lines thin and subtle under zoom.
Always draw the comet glyph for an explicitly selected object such as Halley, regardless of the automatic comet layer's age/range limits or visibility toggle; keep automatic markers filtered.
Add optional pale-cyan nucleus-and-tail comet icons to Sky Compass maps, with a persistent Show comets toggle and date-filtered MPC positions.
Show source filenames, data dates and download timestamps for MPC comets, NASA solar images and cloud imagery, and NOAA space-weather feeds; distinguish observations from retrieval times.
Fix Earth map observer and zoom controls overflowing narrow tablet dashboard cards; wrap by available panel width and verify button-label bounds in Firefox.
Make MPC comets searchable in Sky Compass, with approximate two-body heliocentric propagation, topocentric RA/Dec and Alt/Az, selection marker, Center and Follow, and orbital-accuracy warnings.

Add the official MPC CometEls.txt import foundation, validated offline orbital-element snapshots with source/freshness metadata, and a catalogue status in Sky Compass; comet positions are not yet calculated.
Add Locate me beside Set observer on map, reusing the existing permission-aware browser geolocation to restore current observer coordinates.
Add an explicit Set observer on map crosshair mode; click or tap any visible Earth point to update observer coordinates without changing normal globe rotation behavior.
Show selected-object rise, upper-transit and set times for the simulation UTC date, including circumpolar visibility status and geometric-horizon cautions.
Extend the celestial object finder to all seven visible planets using the same topocentric Astronomy Engine ephemerides as Sky Compass, with date-aware positioning and regression tests.
Move celestial object search into a compact collapsible section within Sky Compass, retaining search, Center and Follow controls and mobile fullscreen access.
Add optional Follow through time tracking for the selected celestial object, with continuous Sky Compass recentering and manual pan/rotation/zoom to exit tracking.
Add a Center in Sky Compass action for selected finder results, repositioning either projection and revealing below-horizon targets in the rectangular view.
Highlight the selected celestial search result in both Sky Compass projections with a date-aware position marker, including zoom-aware sizing.
Introduce an offline celestial object finder for named stars, Messier objects and constellations, with date- and observer-aware RA/Dec, azimuth, altitude and horizon status.
Make below-horizon polar zoom transition smoothly from 1× to 0.5×, progressively revealing the hidden sky while keeping the disc centred and fitting the viewport.
Fit the full below-horizon polar sky to the available canvas in regular and fullscreen layouts, preserving the largest possible view and keeping cursor mapping aligned.

Shift the sub-1× polar sky downward to avoid clipping at the top while preserving its angular scale; keep grids, Milky Way, ecliptic, objects and cursor mapping aligned without altering the normal 1× view.

Extend the polar Sky Compass zoom to 0.5× to reveal the below-horizon hemisphere; distinguish it with a shaded annulus and prominent horizon ring, while retaining the normal 1× view and extending celestial overlays.
Render the Moon in the Sky Compass as a phase-correct illuminated disc, with the bright limb directed toward the Sun in the active sky projection.

Reconcile Earth map projection/style, sky display choices, Orrery settings, sliders and other preference-backed controls with internal state on startup and browser page restoration; add reload regression coverage.
Persist the Orrery 3D checkbox and synchronize its displayed state with the actual camera setting after loading preferences and restoring pages.
Extend Orrery tilt to −90° through +90°, add native touch handling and inclined sampled planetary orbit guides; automatically stamp release-specific service-worker cache identities during packaging.
Reduce Orrery canvas redraw overhead and add mouse-drag regression coverage.
Add drag-to-rotate/tilt Orrery interaction, synchronized camera sliders and a reset-view control; correct the displayed version metadata.
Update Orrery controls to redraw the Orrery directly rather than refreshing the entire dashboard.
Introduce optional 3D Orrery perspective with tilt and rotation sliders.
Group optional Sky Compass layers into collapsible sections and move Milky Way developer diagnostics behind an expandable disclosure. The default sky visualization and controls remain available.
Remove inconsistent state/province text labels while preserving their boundary lines; country names remain for broad orientation and city names for local detail.

Display the nearest catalogued city or town at the selected observer marker with an approximate great-circle distance; the label is prioritised over ordinary map names on all three Earth projections. The worldwide catalog is incomplete, so this is not guaranteed to be the actual nearest settlement.

Expand the offline city catalog to approximately 1,283 world locations using Natural Earth 1:50m populated places, all 50 U.S. state capitals and retained curated entries. City-label eligibility increases with zoom while overlap avoidance limits visible density. The catalog-based observer settlement label arrived in v71.
Remove duplicate Ontario label, prevent duplicate on-screen place labels, and refine font sizes/weights plus eclipse track and center-marker styling.
Introduce Physical, Hybrid and Political Earth styles, offline country and selected state/province boundaries, and zoom-sensitive city labels for all three projections.
Draw the geographic central-shadow footprint for solar eclipses, distinguishing totality from annularity and reporting observer eclipse status.
Improve eclipse track/center visibility and geographic readouts; add Firefox checks for shadow rendering in three Earth projections.
Introduce a simulated solar-eclipse penumbra and central ground track on the Earth map and ±1-minute time stepping.

Eclipse searches now expand over a selected 100–5,000-year horizon instead of fixed 30-year/200-event caps; progressive feedback and cancellation keep the browser usable. Extreme dates are ephemeris-dependent.

Eclipse Explorer with location-aware past/future solar and lunar events, partial/total/penumbral renderings, UTC contacts and event navigator. Solar eclipse images are simulated independently of latest NASA photos; Earth-map paths were added later in v65.
Interactive daylight-year explorer: dated equinox/solstice markers, hover/touch day inspection and daylight gained/lost per day.
Fullscreen keyboard focus fix and 24-hour time displays.
Fullscreen panel browsing with Left/Right keyboard keys and on-screen previous/next buttons; no swipe conflicts.

Solar disc latitude-of-view B₀ projection and P-angle readout; grid anchored to approximate photo retrieval epoch, independent of simulation time. Assumes solar-north-up SDO imagery pending registration.
Keep coordinate overlay physically locked to Sun/Moon images during pan, zoom and reset; remove CSS transform override and add dual-disc Firefox tests.
Align lunar canvas and solar grid with actual visible discs; thinner dark solar lines, adaptive 15-degree grids and denser coordinate labels.

Introduce optional projected reference coordinate grids and pointer/touch readouts for the Sun and Moon. These are educational reference coordinates: exact lunar libration and solar image registration are not yet supported.

Add previous/next planetary opposition, conjunction, quadrature, and Mercury/Venus greatest-elongation navigation; date/time jumps, event details and dashed geometry, with Astronomy Engine orbital coordinates.

Repair final build metadata showing v51, prefer network for PWA navigation/version checks and update existing tabs. Fill genuine black satellite swath gaps with the previous day's NOAA-20/21 observations, labelled as multi-day imagery.
Combine available same-day NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 VIIRS cloud observations per map position to reduce unobserved Pacific swath gaps without fabricating clouds.
Restore cloud imagery after Suomi-NPP's November 2026 retirement, using active NOAA-20 VIIRS with NOAA-21 fallback and explicit satellite identification.
Replace MODIS daily imagery with wider-swath VIIRS/Suomi-NPP imagery to avoid orbital-scan gaps in the cloud overlay.

Optional NASA VIIRS satellite cloud approximation on all Earth map projections; strength control, imagery date, refresh and unavailable status. Daily observed imagery is independent of the simulation clock; not a forecast or measured cloud fraction.
Fix planetary Kp parsing for NOAA's March 2026 JSON format change while preserving legacy responses.
Use grayscale NASA city-light emissions instead of the coloured terrain composite to preserve Earth's natural dark-side appearance.
NOAA OVATION near-real-time auroral forecast overlay and planetary Kp, with night-side NASA Black Marble 2016 city lights. All three Earth projections; timestamps and offline messaging.
Sky Compass checkbox rows wrap within the standard two-column dashboard.
Astronomical Information visible by default; dotted Sun when below the hero chart's horizon.
Generated lakeside twilight panorama integrated into the local/offline PWA.
Observatory-first landing page, large local clock, live solar altitude journey and responsive landscape experiments.
Independent, zoom-aware names for all 88 IAU constellations.
Messier galaxies, nebulae, clusters and optional labels.
Earth projection refinements, coordinate grids, planets in the sky, mobile fullscreen improvements and polar Milky Way fixes.
Sun/Moon imaging and zoom, two sky projections, Milky Way contour accuracy, precession/labels, cursor coordinates, and astronomy-focused regression tests.
Below-horizon celestial chart, almanac, flexible dashboards and early constellation/Milky Way features.
